Solution B is correct. The 12 meals supply food for 18 people, so each meal feeds 18/12 = 3/2 people. To feed 12 people, they need 12 ÷ 3/2 = 8 meals. Solution B reaches this by computing that each person ate 12/18 = 2/3 of a meal, then 2/3 × 12 = 8.

Solution A sets up the proportion correctly as x/12 = 1/(3/2) = 2/3, which gives x = 8. It then cross-multiplies incorrectly, writing 2x = 12 instead of 3x = 24. Its own check also fails: it says 6 meals feed 9 people, which doesn't match the 12 people the problem requires.

WINNER: B
